newsitem.title: USA: Ex-Detroit mayor Young's condition upgraded.
newsitem.headline: Ex-Detroit mayor Young's condition upgraded.

text.p: Former Detroit mayor Coleman Young took a turn for the better in his battle with pneumonia on Wednesday, prompting doctors to upgrade his medical condition from serious to fair at Sinai Hospital.
Young, 79, who has long suffered from emphysema, was admitted to the hospital last week for rehabilitation therapy, but suffered from a recurrence of pneumonia on Monday night, doctors said.
Dr. Marc Dunn said Young remained in the hospital's intensive care unit, but was taken off a respirator and is joking around with nurses.
"Overnight he made great progress, and actually I was surprised, after doing this for so many years, that he made the progress he did overnight," Dunn said. "He's quite a fighter."
Young, the city's first black mayor, retired at the end of 1993 after 20 years in office. A longtime smoker, he has frequently suffered respiratory ailments.
In March 1995, he was in the hospital for 10 days with a minor stroke.
